## Introduction

`tempoPlot` is a package in the `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")` family for
visualizing longitudinal microbiome data. It plots data and results stored
in `TreeSummarizedExperiment` and `MultiAssayExperiment` objects, many of
them computed with `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("miaTime")` and
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("mia")`. All functions return `ggplot` objects.

| Question | Functions |
|---|---|
| When were samples taken? | `plotSwimmer()`, `plotGaps()`, `plotCalendar()` |
| How does a value change over time? | `plotTrend()`, `plotTimeEffect()`, `plotPath()` |
| How does the composition change? | `plotComposition()`, `plotTiles()`, `plotHorizon()`, `plotRanks()`, `plotAlluvial()`, `plotTransitionMatrix()` |
| How fast and how much do communities change? | `plotTurnover()`, `plotTBI()`, `plotRecurrence()`, `plotIndividuality()`, `plotFingerprint()`, `plotLagProfile()` |
| Are there states, rhythms or leads? | `plotLandscape()`, `plotSpectrum()`, `plotLagHeatmap()`, `plotSurvival()` |
| Which features or subjects stand out? | `plotVolcano()`, `plotFeatureScatter()`, `plotStats()`, `plotSubjectScatter()`, `plotTimeLoadings()` |
| How do ordinations and networks compare? | `plotProcrustes()`, `plotDirection()`, `plotNetwork()`, `plotDOC()` |

## Installation

```{r}
#| label: install
#| eval: false

remotes::install_github("0xMuluh/tempoPlot")
```

```{r}
#| label: load

library(tempoPlot)
library(miaTime)
library(mia)
```

The examples use three datasets from miaTime: `hitchip1006`, an adult
cohort sampled up to five times over several years; `minimalgut`, a
defined community of 16 species in three bioreactors sampled every few
hours under the same perturbations; and `SilvermanAGutData`, four
artificial guts sampled daily and hourly.

```{r}
#| label: data

data(hitchip1006)
tse <- hitchip1006
# Some profiles are stored twice; keep the first copy
tse <- tse[, !duplicated(t(assay(tse, "counts")))]
tse <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) >= 3))]
tse$visit <- factor(ave(tse$time, tse$subject, FUN = rank))

data(minimalgut)
mg <- transformAssay(minimalgut, method = "relabundance")
```

## Study design

`plotSwimmer()` shows when each subject was sampled. In `hitchip1006`, the
subjects followed longest are mostly overweight or obese, while those with
short follow-up are mostly lean.

```{r}
#| label: plot-swimmer

plotSwimmer(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject",
    colour.by = "bmi_group")
```

`events` marks interventions as bands (with an `end`) or markers, here the
perturbation schedule shared by the bioreactors. `missing = "show"` marks
gaps longer than `max.gap` with dashed lines.

```{r}
#| label: plot-swimmer-events
#| fig-height: 4

events <- data.frame(
    start = c(0, 152, 432),
    end = c(24, NA, 436),
    label = c("batch", "Blautia added", "double dilution rate"))
plotSwimmer(minimalgut, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    events = events)
```

`plotGaps()` shows the intervals between consecutive samples of each
subject, and `plotCalendar()` the samples per day for `Date` times.

```{r}
#| label: plot-gaps
#| fig-height: 4

plotGaps(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject", group.by = "sex",
    layout = "box")
```

## Trajectories

`plotTrend()` shows one value over time for each subject: a colData
column, such as a result from miaTime, a feature or an ordination
component. Here, the divergence of each subject from their first sample,
computed with `addBaselineDivergence()`, by visit, the order of each
subject's samples. A subject's line breaks at visits without a sample, and
for numeric and `Date` times at gaps longer than `max.gap`.

```{r}
#| label: plot-trend

tse <- addBaselineDivergence(tse, group = "subject", time.col = "time",
    assay.type = "counts")
plotTrend(tse, y = "divergence", time.col = "visit", group = "subject",
    layout = "box")
```

`baseline` expresses a value relative to each subject's first sample, and
`smooth` adds a group summary.

```{r}
#| label: plot-trend-baseline

plotTrend(tse, y = "diversity", time.col = "visit", group = "subject",
    group.by = "sex", baseline = "difference", smooth = "mean")
```

`align.to` draws time relative to an event of each subject. The result is
a ggplot, so further layers can be added, such as the range of acetate
before Blautia hydrogenotrophica was added at 152 h. After the addition,
acetate rose above that range.

```{r}
#| label: plot-trend-align
#| fig-height: 4

minimalgut$added <- 152
before <- range(minimalgut$Acetate[minimalgut$Time_hr_num < 152])
plotTrend(minimalgut, y = "Acetate", time.col = "Time_hr_num",
    group = "StudyIdentifier", group.by = "StudyIdentifier",
    align.to = "added") +
    ggplot2::annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = before[1],
        ymax = before[2], alpha = 0.2)
```

`plotTimeEffect()` draws an effect at each time with its confidence
interval, such as the difference in diversity between men and women at
each visit. Each subject has one sample per visit, so a linear model per
visit compares independent subjects.

```{r}
#| label: plot-time-effect
#| fig-height: 4

cd <- as.data.frame(colData(tse))
effect <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cd, cd$visit), function(d) {
    model <- lm(diversity ~ sex, data = d)
    ci <- confint(model)["sexmale", ]
    data.frame(visit = d$visit[1], estimate = coef(model)[["sexmale"]],
        lower = ci[[1]], upper = ci[[2]])
}))
plotTimeEffect(effect, time.col = "visit")
```

`plotPath()` follows subjects through an ordination or two variables;
`centroids` adds the mean path of each group.

```{r}
#| label: plot-path

tse <- transformAssay(tse, method = "relabundance")
tse <- addMDS(tse, assay.type = "relabundance", method = "bray",
    name = "PCoA")
five <- tse[, tse$subject %in% names(which(table(tse$subject) == 5))]
plotPath(five, time.col = "visit", group = "subject", dimred = "PCoA",
    group.by = "sex", centroids = TRUE)
```

## Composition over time

`plotComposition()` stacks the most abundant features over time, as bars,
areas or a stream; `as.relative = FALSE` stacks absolute values such as
relative abundance times biomass.

```{r}
#| label: plot-composition
#| fig-height: 4

plotComposition(minimalgut, time.col = "Time_hr_num",
    group = "StudyIdentifier", top = 8, layout = "area")
```

`plotTiles()` draws features by time as a heatmap of values, changes,
presence, or effects from a results table. `plotHorizon()` folds each
feature into a short strip, and `plotRanks()` follows the rank of each
feature.

```{r}
#| label: plot-tiles
#| fig-height: 5

plotTiles(mg, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    assay.type = "relabundance", value = "change", order.by = "cluster",
    level = "group")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-horizon
#| fig-height: 5

plotHorizon(mg, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    assay.type = "relabundance", top = 8)
```

States such as the dominant genus are drawn as flows between visits by
`plotAlluvial()` and as transition shares by `plotTransitionMatrix()`.

```{r}
#| label: plot-transitions
#| fig-height: 5

h <- addDominant(hitchip1006, name = "dominant", n = 4)
plotTransitionMatrix(h, state.col = "dominant", time.col = "time",
    group = "subject")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-alluvial
#| fig-height: 5
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("ggalluvial", quietly = TRUE)

h$visit <- ave(h$time, h$subject, FUN = rank)
h <- h[, h$visit <= 3 & h$subject %in% names(which(table(h$subject) >= 2))]
h$visit <- factor(h$visit)
plotAlluvial(h, state.col = "dominant", time.col = "visit",
    group = "subject")
```

## Change and stability

`plotTurnover()` counts the features gained and lost between consecutive
samples; `plotTBI()` splits the change between two time points into losses
and gains (Legendre 2019), here of genera present or absent.

```{r}
#| label: plot-tbi
#| fig-height: 5

plotTBI(tse, time.col = "visit", group = "subject", time.point = c("1", "2"),
    colour.by = "sex")
```

From a dissimilarity stored by `addDissimilarity()`, `plotRecurrence()`
draws the dissimilarities between the samples of each subject over time,
`plotIndividuality()` compares them with those between subjects, and
`plotFingerprint()` asks whether each subject's later sample is closest to
its own earlier one.

```{r}
#| label: plot-recurrence
#| fig-height: 4

mg <- addDissimilarity(mg, method = "bray", assay.type = "counts")
plotRecurrence(mg, dissimilarity = "bray", time.col = "Time.hr",
    group = "StudyIdentifier")
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-individuality
#| fig-height: 4

tse <- addDissimilarity(tse, method = "bray", assay.type = "counts")
plotIndividuality(tse, dissimilarity = "bray", group = "subject")
```

`plotLagProfile()` draws the variogram of `addVariogram()`: how far apart
samples of a subject are, by the time between them.

## States, rhythms and leads

`plotLandscape()` draws the density of a variable or its potential; the
abundance of Prevotella at the first sample of each subject has two wells,
a low and a high state (Lahti et al. 2014).

```{r}
#| label: plot-landscape
#| fig-height: 4

first <- hitchip1006[, hitchip1006$time == 0]
first <- transformAssay(first, method = "relabundance")
first <- transformAssay(first, assay.type = "relabundance",
    method = "log10", pseudocount = 1e-4, name = "log10")
plotLandscape(first, y = "Prevotella melaninogenica et rel.",
    assay.type = "log10", scale = "potential")
```

`plotSpectrum()` finds periodic changes. Acetate in the bioreactors, which
were fasted once a day, has peaks near one cycle per 24 h.

```{r}
#| label: plot-spectrum
#| fig-height: 4

plotSpectrum(minimalgut, y = "Acetate", time.col = "Time_hr_num",
    group = "StudyIdentifier")
```

`plotLagHeatmap()` correlates features with a target at lags of a few
samples.

```{r}
#| label: plot-lag-heatmap
#| fig-height: 5

clr <- transformAssay(minimalgut, method = "clr", pseudocount = 1)
plotLagHeatmap(clr, target = "Acetate", time.col = "Time.hr",
    group = "StudyIdentifier", assay.type = "clr")
```

`plotSurvival()` draws the time until an event, here until the dominant
genus of each subject first changes.

```{r}
#| label: plot-survival
#| fig-height: 4

tse <- addDominant(tse, name = "dominant")
plotSurvival(tse, time.col = "time", group = "subject",
    event = "state.exit", state.col = "dominant", group.by = "sex")
```

## Features and subjects

`plotFeatureScatter()` draws two statistics per feature with a fit, such as
Taylor's law of mean and variance.

```{r}
#| label: plot-feature-scatter
#| fig-height: 4

plotFeatureScatter(first, x.stat = "mean", y.stat = "variance",
    fit = "power")
```

`plotVolcano()` and `plotStats()` draw results per feature, such as the
bimodality of each genus computed by miaTime.

```{r}
#| label: plot-stats
#| fig-height: 4

tse <- addBimodality(tse, assay.type = "counts")
plotStats(tse, stat = "bimodality", top = 20, colour.by = "Phylum")
```

`plotSubjectScatter()` draws two statistics per subject, or the subject
loadings of a tensor decomposition, and `plotTimeLoadings()` its time
loadings. Here the TEMPTED decomposition of the bioreactors (Shi et al.
2024), if the tempted package is installed.

```{r}
#| label: plot-time-loadings
#| fig-height: 4
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("tempted", quietly = TRUE)

counts <- t(assay(minimalgut, "counts"))
metadata(minimalgut)$tempted <- tempted::tempted_all(counts,
    timepoint = minimalgut$Time_hr_num,
    subjectID = as.character(minimalgut$StudyIdentifier), r = 2,
    threshold = 1, pseudo = 0.5, do_ratio = FALSE)
plotTimeLoadings(minimalgut, source = "tempted")
```

## Ordinations and networks

`plotProcrustes()` superimposes two ordinations of the same samples,
`plotDirection()` draws the directions in which subjects move in one,
`plotNetwork()` draws feature or sample networks, and `plotDOC()` the
dissimilarity-overlap curve.

```{r}
#| label: plot-direction
#| fig-height: 4

mg <- addMDS(mg, assay.type = "relabundance", method = "bray",
    name = "PCoA")
plotDirection(mg, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    dimred = "PCoA", facet.by = "StudyIdentifier")
```

## Combining plots

All functions return `ggplot` objects, so the
`r BiocStyle::CRANpkg("patchwork")` package stacks them over a shared time
axis, here for one bioreactor.

```{r}
#| label: combine-plots
#| fig-height: 7
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("patchwork", quietly = TRUE)

library(patchwork)
a <- minimalgut[, minimalgut$StudyIdentifier == "Bioreactor A"]
plotTrend(a, y = "Acetate", time.col = "Time_hr_num") /
    plotComposition(a, time.col = "Time_hr_num", top = 8, layout = "area") /
    plotTurnover(a, time.col = "Time_hr_num") +
    plot_layout(axes = "collect")
```

## References

Lahti L, et al. (2014). Tipping elements in the human intestinal
ecosystem. *Nature Communications* 5:4344.

Legendre P (2019). A temporal beta-diversity index to identify sites that
have changed in exceptional ways in space-time surveys. *Ecology and
Evolution* 9(6):3500-3514.

Shi P, et al. (2024). TEMPTED: time-informed dimensionality reduction for
longitudinal microbiome studies. *Genome Biology* 25:317.
